Sometimes Kai wished his wings were not so small. He was a kitten with wings, and he lived in a warm box behind the bakery.

One cold autumn evening, he saw the green light. It sat on a roof across the town. It was dim, like a sleepy eye.

The green light called to him. He flapped and flapped. He could not reach it.

He found a flower by the road. It was not sparkly. It did not help.

The green light stayed far away. Kai felt a pull in his chest. He jumped and he fell. He tried and he tried.

"Come back," said his mother. "The box is warm."

But the green light was there. The green light was always there. Dim. Sleepy. Far.

Kai sat on a fence and watched the green light. He forgot his dinner. He forgot his name. The wind was cold.

Then his mother licked his head. "Little one," she said. "Some lights are just for looking."

Kai looked one more time at the green light. Then he walked home.

stories.text: Sometimes a kitten with wings is born. Kai was that kitten. His wings were small and soft. He lived in a warm box by a flower shop. One cold autumn evening, he saw a green light. It was on a roof across the town. The green light was dim, like a sleepy eye. Kai felt a pull in his chest. He wanted to reach the green light. He jumped up on a fence. He flapped his little wings. The wind was cold. His wings were not strong yet. He fell down. He tried again. The green light blinked far away. It was sparkly and far. Kai forgot his warm box. He forgot his dinner. He only saw the green light. He walked and walked. His paws got cold. The green light stayed far. It was always far. At last, Kai sat down. He looked at the green light. It was pretty. But it was just a light. He turned back home. The moral is this: some lights are lovely to see, but home is warmer than any green light.

Then Kai saw the green light. It was on a roof across the town. The green light was dim, like a sleepy eye.

Kai stood up. The kitten’s wings went sparkly. A pull came inside Kai. It pulled hard.

“Come back,” said Kai. But the green light blinked. Kai walked. The green light stayed far.

Kai went down the lane. The green light was there. Kai crossed the square. The green light was there. Kai climbed a wall. The green light was still across the town.

The kitten with wings flew behind. It mewed. Kai did not turn.

Green light, green light. Kai reached. Green light, green light. Kai ran. Green light, green light. The cold bit Kai’s hands. Green light, green light. The roof was dark. Green light, green light. The sleepy eye stayed dim.

Kai fell. The kitten landed on Kai’s chest. Warm wings. Warm fur.

Kai looked up. The green light was small and far. It would always be far.

Kai held the flower. The green light did not come close. Some lights are for seeing, not for having.

stories.text: When Eli made a cake with no candles, he put on his tall hat and smiled. He did not need a wish to blow out. He just wanted to share. He cut a slice for his mom. He cut a slice for his dad. They ate it in the late at night dark. The cake was sweet and soft. Then Eli looked out the window. Across the town, on a roof, he saw a green light. It looked as green as a frog. It blinked once. Eli felt a small pull in his chest. He wanted to touch it. But he did not know how. He turned back to his happy family. They laughed and ate more cake. The green light stayed far away. Eli took off his hat. He knew some things are just for looking. You can be happy with what you have. That is the best wish of all.

It was as green as a frog. It blinked far away. Eli wanted to reach it. He wanted to make his wish there. But he could not. The green light stayed far. So Eli put jam on the cake. He gave it to his friend. They ate and felt happy. The green light still blinked across the town. Eli did not need it. A wish is not in a candle. A wish is in your heart.

stories.text: When Eli made a cake with no candles, he did not feel sad. He put on his soft hat. He said, "I do not need a wish tonight." The cake was warm and sweet. He ate one piece alone. Then he looked out his window. Far away, on a roof across the town, he saw the green light. It was as green as a frog. Late at night, it blinked and blinked. Eli turned back to his cake. He took one more bite. But his eyes found the green light again. He pulled his hat down low. "I am happy," he said. The words felt small. He tried to think of his cake. He tried to think of his bed. Still, the green light stayed on the roof. It was as green as a frog. He leaned on the glass. "One small wish," he whispered. The green light did not move. It never came closer. Eli sat down. He ate the last piece. The green light kept shining. He knew it would shine all night. Some things we want stay far away. That is why we must love what is near.

The green light stayed far away. The cake sat alone. Then Eli stopped. He looked at the cake with no candles. He did not need the green light to make a wish. He could wish for one small happy thing right here. So he did. The moral is this: a wish can live in your own hands, not only in a green light far off.

His mother said, “Eli, eat your cake.”

But Eli looked at the green light. Green light. Green light. The cake got cold. The green light did not come closer.

His mother kissed his head. “You can be happy here,” she said.

Eli looked at the green light one more time. Then he took a bite of cake. It was good.

The green light stayed on the roof. Eli smiled. A wish is not always a thing you can reach. Sometimes it is just a light to love from far away.

Rain fell on Kai's window. He sat on the floor with his puzzle. It was a puzzle of a big boat. But one piece was gone. Kai looked under the bed. He looked in his sock drawer. He looked in a puddle by the door. No piece. He felt sad. He wanted to rest. But he wanted to finish the boat more.

Kai put on his coat. He was brave. He walked down the street. The sun was going down. Across the town, on a roof, he saw the green light. It was dim, like a sleepy eye. He looked at the green light for a moment. Then he kept walking.

His friend Mia had the piece. She found it in her bag. Kai said thank you. He went home and put the piece in. The boat was done.

But Mia moved away that night. Kai sat by the puzzle alone. The green light blinked far away.

Then Kai saw the green light. It was on a roof across the town. The green light was dim, like a sleepy eye. The sun was going down. Kai stood up.

"I will be brave," he said. He walked past the puddle. He walked and walked.

He did not find the piece. The green light stayed far away. Kai went home. He put the puzzle away.

The boat would always have a hole. Kai sat by the window. The green light blinked once. Then it was dark.

“I will be brave,” said Kai. “I will get the green light.”

Kai climbed a wall. Kai climbed a tree. The green light stayed far away. Kai thought of the green light. Green light, green light, green light.

Then Kai found the puzzle piece. It was in Kai’s sock. The cat was whole.

But Kai did not care. Kai only looked at the green light. The sun went down. The green light blinked out.

Kai held the piece. Kai felt sad. The puzzle was done. The green light was gone.
